source.title: Face Identity Unlearning for Retrieval via Embedding Dispersion

page_placements.theme: Useful internal information can survive corrupted predictions

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses Random Labeling as an unlearning baseline and reports its effects on face retrieval and identity metrics. It does not measure whether the model fits the randomized labels.
record.gate_note: Random Labeling is applied to the forget set as an unlearning method, with a retain-set loss. The reported outcomes concern original-label accuracy, retrieval, and cluster compactness, not training error on the randomized labels. No results test the claim versions. Cited findings from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Random Labeling is an unlearning baseline applied to a pretrained face encoder's forget subset, alongside a retain-set loss. Tables 1–3 measure retrieval, original-identity accuracy and embedding compactness, not training error on randomized labels. Appendix A varies unlearning settings but likewise reports no random-label fitting measure. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' Random Labeling finding: original-identity accuracy collapses without substantial disruption of cluster compactness or retrieval. The paper's broader conclusion is that existing unlearning baselines struggle with retrieval-based forgetting, whereas the proposed dispersion losses improve forgetting while largely preserving retention utility.
record.recipe_differences: Randomly relabels only the forget set for face identity unlearning, while retaining a loss on non-forgotten data; adapted to a CosFace embedding model. It does not test the original random-label fitting recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports a lightweight hyperparameter search for Random Labeling, with outcomes varying across retain-loss weights and iteration counts (Appendix A, Table 5).

fits_no_version.finding: Random Labeling reduces forgotten-identity test accuracy from 98.20% to 0.00%, while compactness remains 0.615 and base retrieval R@1 remains 98.17%. Base mAP changes from 88.70% to 87.73%; extended mAP changes from 88.40% to 85.87%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this face-unlearning setup, random-label fine-tuning can destroy original-identity classification accuracy while leaving identity clusters and retrieval largely intact.

record.peer_reviewed: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
record.problems: The study does not report training accuracy on the randomized labels, so it cannot establish whether the model fits them. Random Labeling results use a forget-set unlearning setup with a retain-set loss, and the main results average over three sampled forget sets. No chance-level test-error comparison for random labels is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix A, Table 5 reports many single-forget-set Random Labeling hyperparameter configurations. These were left out because they are unlearning outcomes rather than measurements of fitting randomized labels; the retained rows capture the main reported Random Labeling outcomes.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on a completely randomized training set, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance across a label-corruption sweep.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: All twelve rows report baseline-method outcomes outside the claim versions; their values and baselines match the supplied tables. They supply context for fits_no_version, not evidence for claim verdicts. Appendix A's omitted configurations are already declared in rows_left_out and add no measurements bearing on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, with test error at chance and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Training and test performance across a sweep from no label noise to fully random labels.
Whether regularization or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

tranche.reason: Random relabeling is used as an unlearning baseline; reported outcomes measure retrieval, original-identity accuracy and cluster compactness, without measuring fit to randomized training labels.

source_check.notes: Uncertainties summarize three independently sampled forget sets. Zero original-identity test accuracy does not establish fitting randomized training labels; the excerpts and authors' conclusion accurately describe the retrieval findings.
